characters.name: Renate Ward
characters.goal: determine the true cause of the ferry sinking before the provincial inquiry names her

characters.name: Tomas Orlov
characters.goal: keep the crossing open and deflect blame from municipal management

characters.name: Kester Finch
characters.goal: clear his name of negligence in the ferry sinking

characters.name: Gideon Pell
characters.goal: identify criminal culpability for the ferry sinking

characters.name: Barnaby Doolan
characters.status: defensive and smelling of pine pitch
characters.goal: protect his municipal repair contract and slipway license

characters.name: Briony Cole
characters.goal: hold the district authorities accountable for her brother's drowning

characters.name: Marta Ward
characters.goal: maintain household stability and protect Renate's employment

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes the sudden disaster and places Renate's official permit under imminent legal scrutiny.
required_beats: Tomas informs Renate that the crossing barge sank in calm water and Skipper Cole drowned.
Tomas warns Renate that her signature on the permit will draw provincial scrutiny.
Renate resolves to inspect the site before auditors arrive.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Confronts Renate with direct blame and contradictory physical claims regarding the cause of the sinking.
required_beats: Kester Finch describes pressurized water and silt bursting through the bilge floorboards.
Briony Cole accuses Renate and district authorities of causing her brother's death.
Renate notes Kester's belief that a submerged snag punctured the hull.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Escalates the stakes by bringing provincial authority to bear on the river crossing and targeting inspector liability.
required_beats: Prefect Pell impounds the crossing ledgers to investigate criminal liability.
Pell demands the drought-summer inspection certifications.
Tomas pleads to run replacement boats, but Pell halts all river licenses.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Reveals Renate's vulnerability and drives her to protect her household by deflecting fault away from the inspection.
required_beats: Renate examines her permit copy and remembers Barney Doolan's remark about the hull patch needing shade.
Marta reminds Renate that their livelihood and medicine depend on her inspector's post.
Renate resolves to prove operational fault to deflect blame from her inspection.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes the personal and legal jeopardy Renate faces for her afloat inspection of the ferry.
required_beats: Pell interrogates Renate under oath about certifying the ferry afloat without drydock slipway hauling.
Renate defends her afloat sign-off citing district budget limits and river schedules.
Pell warns Renate of penal liability if structural failure caused the disaster.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Redirects Renate's investigation from structural timber defects to the ferry's operational loading.
required_beats: Renate questions Barney Doolan about the replacement hull strakes on the barge.
Barney admits to using green ash instead of cured oak due to provincial budget cutbacks.
Barney defends the green ash repairs and urges Renate to investigate Tomas's cargo loading instead.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Provides Renate with crucial witness evidence that the ferry was dangerously overloaded under threat of dismissal.
required_beats: Briony Cole informs Renate of her brother's argument with Tomas over loading heavy ironstone wagons.
Briony gives Renate her brother's tally card documenting double the permitted cargo.
Renate deduces that Tomas deliberately violated weight limits to pocket toll profits.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Confronts Renate with direct blackmail after she secures documentary proof of Tomas's cargo fraud.
required_beats: Renate uncovers hidden carbon slips in the wharf office proving Tomas halved reported freight weights.
Tomas catches Renate with the evidence and threatens to revoke her sister's medical stipend.
Renate defies Tomas's blackmail to preserve the proof that will clear her name.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes the river depth over the gravel spit, setting up the collision theory Renate relies on to explain the sinking.
required_beats: Renate uses a weighted sounding pole over the gravel spit and confirms four feet of water clearance.
Kester argues that sixteen tons of cargo would have forced the barge to strike the bottom.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Renate stakes her defense on overloading and grounding, prompting Pell to order the hull raised to examine physical damage.
required_beats: Pell opens the hearing, where Renate announces she has proof the disaster was caused by operational overloading.
Renate presents the doctored manifest showing sixteen tons of ironstone, arguing it grounded the barge on the gravel spit.
Pell orders the hull raised from the river to verify bottom impact damage.
Tomas has Barney Doolan confirm Renate certified the framing for twenty tons, leaving Renate dependent on finding impact marks on the keel.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Dismantles Renate's grounding theory and reveals the true mechanical cause of the hull failure.
required_beats: The waterlogged hull is winched onto the riverbank skids before the gathered crowd.
Renate scrapes the silt from the oak keel and discovers no impact damage or gouges, disproving the collision theory.
Pell warns Renate that without collision evidence, she faces responsibility for a spontaneous hull failure.
Renate inspects the starboard planks and realizes green wood baked and shrank in the drought sun, allowing water and silt to burst through the seams.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Exposes Renate's complicity in ignoring known structural risks to maintain the ferry crossing.
required_beats: Renate confronts Barney Doolan with shrunken green ash splinters taken from the failed seam.
Barney admits he installed green ash and warned Renate it would check if left to dry in the sun.
Barney reminds Renate she suppressed his warning on her official certificate to keep the ferry operational.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Renate commits to sacrificing her livelihood and security by confessing her negligence to Marta and preparing her sworn statement.
required_beats: Renate admits to Marta that she ignored Barney's warning about the green ash to secure her inspector voucher.
Marta tearfully concedes that remaining silent would endanger other river crews on green-patched boats.
Renate writes out her sworn statement admitting she certified the vessel despite the improper timber.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Renate delivers her damning confession before the inquiry, accepting total professional ruin to prevent further river drownings.

char_renate_ward.goal: determine the true cause of the ferry sinking before the provincial inquiry names her
survive the penal trial and secure Marta's welfare

required_beats: Renate testifies under oath that she concealed the green ash warning and explains how the drought caused the seams to fail.
Pell orders all municipal craft patched with green ash to be condemned and grounded immediately.
Pell revokes Renate's credentials, strips her allowances, and binds her over for trial.
Briony Cole acknowledges Renate's honesty in refusing to blame the dead skipper.
Renate watches the silent river crossing, reconciling her family's ruin with having saved the district crews.

metadata.title: The Low Water Mark
metadata.source: segmented from a Fabula-only package by gemini-3.8-flash

premise.logline: A river ferry sinks in calm water, and the woman who signed off on its last inspection has to find out why before the inquiry does.

modules.theme: what a person will certify to keep a job that feeds other people
modules.setting_time: a drought summer, in a country with more paperwork than money
modules.setting_place: a river crossing town that exists because the ferry does
modules.protagonist: the district inspector who signed the ferry fit to sail
modules.protagonist_want: to find the real cause before the inquiry names her as it
modules.antagonism: the people who need the ferry running more than they need it safe
modules.complication: the cause turns out to be something she was told about and did not write down
modules.ending_shape: the truth is established and costs the person who established it

plot_shape.name: Mystery
plot_shape.central_question: What actually happened, and who is willing to say so?

phases.name: Disturbance
phases.purpose: A wrong surfaces and someone is obliged to look into it.

phases.name: Inquiry
phases.purpose: Evidence accumulates, most of it true and misread.

phases.name: Wrong turn
phases.purpose: A reading of the evidence that is coherent and wrong collapses.

phases.name: Solution
phases.purpose: The true account, assembled only from what the reader has already been shown.

phases.name: Cost
phases.purpose: What knowing costs the person who found out.

cast_roles.purpose: Carries the reader through the inquiry and pays its cost.
Has a reason to keep the true account from being assembled.
Holds one true piece and misunderstands its meaning.
The reason the question matters at all.

obligatory_moves: Every element of the true account is on the page before it is stated.
At least one true detail is shown early in a context that makes it look irrelevant.
The wrong reading is defensible on the evidence available when it is made.

events.summary: Renate arrives at the wharf office where Tomas announces the crossing barge sank in calm water and Skipper Cole drowned.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance phase begins; establishes the disaster and the institutional pressure on Renate's inspection sign-off.
beats: Tomas informs Renate that The Oarman sank without warning three hundred yards out in slack current.
Tomas warns Renate that her inspection signature on the permit will be scrutinized by the provincial magistrates.
Renate commits to examining the site immediately before official auditors arrive.

events.summary: At the riverbank, deckhand Kester Finch insists that river water erupted through the bilge floorboards like an inward explosion.
events.dramatic_function: Witness statement introduces the critical physical anomaly under a flawed interpretation.
beats: Kester Finch describes pressurized river silt shooting upward through the bottom floorboards before the deck flooded.
Briony Cole confronts Renate, blaming district negligence for her brother's drowning.
Renate records Kester's conviction that the barge struck a sunken river snag that punctured the bottom.

events.summary: Prefect Gideon Pell arrives from the provincial capital to impound all crossing ledgers and initiate an inquiry.
events.dramatic_function: Introduces the antagonist investigator and raises the ticking clock stakes.
beats: Gideon Pell announces he will hold formal hearings to assign individual criminal responsibility.
Pell demands all inspection certifications signed during the drought summer.
Tomas petitions Pell to let replacement freight boats operate, but Pell freezes all crossing licenses.

events.summary: At home, Renate reviews her inspection copy and recalls an unrecorded remark by Barney Doolan about the hull repair.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance concludes; protagonist realizes she omitted vital spoken information to protect her job.
beats: Renate studies her stamped certificate and recalls Barney mentioning on inspection day that the repair patch needed shade.
Marta reminds Renate that losing the inspector's salary would leave them unable to pay for her tinctures.
Renate decides to find external operational faults to ensure the inspection itself is not blamed.

events.summary: Pell formally examines Renate under oath regarding her decision to certify the ferry without requiring drydock slipway hauling.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry phase begins; formal pressure on the protagonist's procedural shortcuts.
beats: Pell questions Renate on why she signed off on The Oarman afloat rather than ordering it onto the drydock slipway.
Renate defends her afloat inspection by citing district budget directives and low river schedules.
Pell warns Renate that certifying craft without slipway inspection carries penal liability if structural flaws caused the sinking.

events.summary: Renate questions shipwright Barney Doolan, who grumbles about being forced to use unseasoned green ash for municipal repairs.
events.dramatic_function: Plants the true material cause while framing it as everyday repair yard grievance.
beats: Renate questions Barney regarding the hull strakes replaced during the recent overhaul.
Barney complains that the provincial timber cutbacks forced him to plank the barge with green ash instead of cured oak.
Barney insists green ash swells water-tight anyway and directs Renate to look at how Tomas loads the wagons.

events.summary: Briony Cole tells Renate that her brother loudly argued with Tomas against loading heavy ironstone wagons that morning.
events.dramatic_function: Witness information guides the investigation toward the plausible overloading theory.
beats: Briony reveals her brother refused to depart until Tomas threatened him with dismissal over the ironstone cargo.
Briony hands Renate her brother's tally card showing twice the permitted wagon count.
Renate realizes Tomas may have bypassed municipal cargo limits to pocket extra crossing tolls.

events.summary: Renate searches the wharf office alone and finds carbon duplicates showing Tomas halved the reported weight of ironstone freight.
events.dramatic_function: Uncovers hard documentary evidence supporting the incorrect overloading hypothesis.
beats: Renate unseals the tollkeeper's lockbox in the wharf office.
She discovers scale receipts proving sixteen tons of crushed ironstone were loaded under an eight-ton manifest entry.
Renate pockets the carbon slips to build a case of catastrophic overloading against Tomas.

events.summary: Tomas catches Renate with the receipts and threatens to terminate the town medical stipend for her invalid sister.
events.dramatic_function: Antagonist exerts direct coercion, highlighting the story's core dilemma between livelihood and truth.
beats: Tomas intercepts Renate leaving the desk with the carbon records.
Tomas bluntly states that Marta's clinic stipend is drawn from crossing revenues he controls.
Renate refuses to surrender the slips, convinced the cargo fraud will exonerate her inspection.

events.summary: Renate and Kester measure the river channel and confirm the gravel spit had four feet of water clearance at the time of sinking.
events.dramatic_function: Collects hydrological data that sets up the eventual collapse of the grounding theory.
beats: Renate uses a weighted sounding pole along the ferry's plotted track over the gravel spit.
The depth sounding shows four full feet of water over the gravel bar crest, ample for standard unladen draft.
Kester argues that sixteen tons of ironstone would have pushed the barge bottom straight onto the gravel ridge.

events.summary: Gideon Pell orders an open court session to hear technical submissions, and Renate announces she has proof of the disaster's cause.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry phase concludes; Renate commits fully to her mistaken thesis.
beats: Pell gives formal notice that findings of criminal negligence will be entered within twenty-four hours.
Renate declares she possesses documentary proof that operational overloading caused the loss.
Tomas angrily protests that Renate is concocting excuses to protect her inspector badge.

events.summary: Before Magistrate Pell, Renate presents the doctored manifest and claims ironstone weight broke the barge on the gravel spit.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong turn phase begins; the coherent but incorrect reading is presented formally.
beats: Renate submits the hidden weigh-station carbons proving sixteen tons of cargo on deck.
Renate argues that the excess weight grounded the vessel on the gravel spit, breaching the hull bottom.
Pell agrees the paper evidence is compelling but orders the hull winched from the river to verify bottom impact damage.

events.summary: Tomas calls Barney Doolan to testify that Renate's certified rating permitted twenty tons of deck weight if sound.
events.dramatic_function: Heightens tension in the wrong turn by exposing the vulnerability of Renate's argument.
beats: Barney Doolan confirms under oath that Renate certified the framing for twenty tons capacity.
Tomas argues that sixteen tons should have sailed safely unless the inspector overlooked underlying rot.
Renate realizes her accusation hinges entirely on physical proof of a violent stone impact on the keel.

events.summary: Municipal winches drag the waterlogged hull of The Oarman out of the tidal mud and onto the riverbank skids.
events.dramatic_function: The physical body of the vessel is made accessible for inspection.
beats: Capstans and draft horses drag the barge hull clear of the low-tide river mud.
Water pours out of the open hold while townsfolk gather to inspect the drowned craft.
Renate readies her scraper and lantern to locate the expected impact breach along the keel.

events.summary: Renate scrapes the raised hull bottom and finds the keel unbroken, proving the barge never struck the gravel spit.
events.dramatic_function: Collapse of the wrong turn; the overloading-impact hypothesis is completely disproven.
beats: Renate scrapes silt from the entire length of the oak keel and finds zero gouges or splintering.
Pell notes that the four-foot channel clearance held true, meaning no ground collision ever happened.
Pell warns Renate that without collision damage, the vessel failed by spontaneous hull breach under her certification.

events.summary: Renate discovers the starboard planks shrank and pulled from their spikes in the drought heat, creating the gaps that burst with silt.
events.dramatic_function: Solution phase begins; the true physical mechanism is deduced from observed material facts.
beats: Renate inspects the starboard strakes and finds wide open seams where planks checked and warped along the grain.
She realizes the unseasoned green wood baked in the triple-digit drought sun on the dock, shrinking away from fastenings.
When weighted with cargo, water pressure violently forced silt up through the shrunken seams, creating Kester's 'blast'.

events.summary: Renate confronts Barney Doolan at his timberyard, forcing him to admit he installed green ash and warned her about it.
events.dramatic_function: Solution phase links the material failure to human culpability and Renate's omitted note.
beats: Renate presents Barney with shrunken green ash splinters extracted from the open seam.
Barney admits he told her during inspection that green ash planks would check if left dry in the sun.
Barney reminds Renate that she deliberately omitted his warning from her official certificate to keep the crossing running.

events.summary: Renate returns home to tell Marta she will testify to the truth of her own negligence, knowing it will cost her job and pension.
events.dramatic_function: Solution phase concludes with the conscious ethical choice to accept devastating personal loss.
beats: Renate confesses to Marta that she ignored Barney's warning about the green ash to ensure her inspector voucher cleared.
Marta tearfully accepts that staying silent would leave other green-patched district boats to drown more men.
Renate writes out her sworn statement admitting she certified the vessel knowing green timber had been fitted.

events.summary: Before the full inquiry hall, Renate testifies under oath that she omitted the warning about green ash from her certification.
events.dramatic_function: Cost phase begins; the truth is formally established at the protagonist's direct expense.
beats: Renate submits her revised testimony, admitting she received verbal warning about green ash and omitted it from the log.
She shows how drought heat shrank the unseasoned wood above the waterline until loading pulled the seams open.
Pell orders an emergency grounding and condemnation of every municipal craft patched with green ash.

events.summary: Pell strips Renate of her inspector's seal and binds her over for trial, while Briony acknowledges the truth of her brother's drowning.
events.dramatic_function: Cost phase concludes; protagonist bears the consequences of her confession while justice is recorded.
beats: Pell revokes Renate's inspector credential, strips her of all salary and medical allowances, and orders her held for trial.
Briony Cole speaks to Renate outside the rail, recognizing that Renate told the truth when she could have blamed the dead skipper.
Renate watches the crossing shuttered and silent, knowing she saved the river crews even as she ruined her own family.

state_changes.value: survive the penal trial and secure Marta's welfare

vacuous_checks: entry_exit_contradiction — entry_state is derived from the same replay that produces exit_state (src/segmentation/state.ts), so consecutive scenes agree by construction
plant_not_declared — every accepted plant/payoff pair writes its fact into the plant scene's own reader_must_learn as it is applied
unpaid_fact — reader_must_learn is populated only from facts that some scene pays off
